title: 26 · chandesha · The Boy Steward
lines: n
A man once kicked his own son's Shiva lingam.
n
The boy never even opened his eyes.
n
He was a cowherd. Seven years old.
The cows loved him so much, they gave more milk than anyone could carry.
n
So with the milk nobody needed,
he built a lingam of sand by the river, and bathed it. Every day.
n
The villagers saw milk running into the sand.
He is wasting it, they told his father.
"He is wasting it," they told his father.
n
His father hid behind a tree, and watched.
n
Then he walked out, shouting.
The boy did not hear.
So he kicked the pots.
n
The boy's hand found a stick, and swung.
He never looked to see who he was striking.
n
And when he opened his eyes, his father had fallen,
and Shiva and Parvati were standing in the river.
s
For my sake you forgot even your father.
From today, I am your father.
n
He restored the old man,
and gave the boy the keys to everything offered to him.
n
That is why, in a Shiva temple, you stop at one small shrine before you leave, with empty hands.
n
Give your whole attention, or none. That is sadhana.
n
